region.finding: Actually inspected all 24 enlarged source/battle head and whole-body front/side slices, all 13 clips at six phases. Bamboo Ape upper face, eyes, hair and headband retain shape, but the tooth bar, lower lip/chin and black side jaw pull toward the coat during idle_2, hit, death and victory head tilts. Arms, hands, belt, legs, toes and bamboo back prop remain coherent. Independent landmark drift confirms incomplete lower-face bindings; second visual pass and candidate comparison required.

Actually inspected all 24 enlarged source/battle head and whole-body front/side slices, all 13 clips at six phases. Frostbite Cub cheek and muzzle visibly balloon in walk/gallop/attack then squash into sharp creases during jump and hit; death also pulls the lower face into the scarf. Eyes and forehead remain comparatively steady. Body clothing, arms, paws, legs and curled tail remain coherent. Both assets have the same clear lower-face defect; candidate must preserve mobile scarf while stabilizing the face.

Actually inspected all 24 enlarged source/battle head and whole-body front/side slices, all 13 clips at six phases. Shrine Salamander eyes, muzzle and side cheek look stable at these sampled poses; no dramatic facial distortion observed. Numerical independent lower-face probe identifies one source chin vertex with non-head influence and 0.00889 drift; battle patch passes. A small front-chin binding correction will be compared before acceptance. Scarf folds, head ties, four limbs, digits, torso, tail and flame stay coherent.

Actually inspected all 24 enlarged source/battle head and whole-body front/side slices, all 13 clips at six phases. Granite Badger white cheek, eyes and nose stay mostly steady, with a subtle lower black jaw/muzzle shear when the head tilts away from the scarf in idle_2, hit and death. Independent source/battle lower-face drift confirms missing binding. Scarf is cloth and must retain its movement; hands, arms, padded torso, legs, feet, tail and back weapon show no separate tearing.

Actually inspected all 24 enlarged source/battle head and whole-body front/side slices, all 13 clips at six phases. Young Direwolf lower white muzzle and dark jaw subtly change their relation to the nose/eyes during idle_2, jump, death and victory head tilts; the side jaw is pulled toward the blue scarf. Independent source/battle probes confirm the defect. Ears, crown fur, body mane, four legs, paws and short tail remain coherent. Candidate must hold the complete muzzle without freezing the scarf or chest fur.
